title: Guise? to the duc de Mercœur, 27 May and 20 June 1587, BnF fr. 15564 ff. 119 and 142 (DECODE R4162, R4165)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 15564 f. 142 (Gallica btv1b9064027v, view 155 right); DECODE R4165

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the slip; no plaintext published.

transcription.notes: Seven clear lines, then 16 lines of cipher; several similar signs merged under one label at first pass.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution (2-7 signs per letter: cursive letter-forms, digits, Greek-like signs) plus a small nomenclator of ff-ligature groups for common words and digit groups for names; no word division.
system.sibling_key: Lasry 2022 key for fr. 15564 ff. 27/78/119/142 and fr. 15565 ff. 105/122 (cryptiana GL.htm, GL_BnFfr15564.png).
system.notes: Several signs are near-identical shapes with different values (loop = A or S; C-shape = L, R or F); the reading resolves them by context.

prior_solution.where: George Lasry's key table (2022) on cryptiana GL.htm names ff. 119 and 142 among the letters it solves; no plaintext published; DECODE records still 'Non-decrypted'.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5 and posed the catalogue entry with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R4162/R4165 metadata with the saved cookie: they are fr. 15564 ff. 119 and 142.
cryptiana GL.htm: Lasry's 2022 key covers ff. 27, 78, 119, 142; downloaded the key table and his f. 27 decipherment image.
Located f. 119 (view 132) and f. 142 (view 155) on Gallica and fetched full-resolution crops.
First-pass glyph-label transcription of f. 142's 16 cipher lines (574 signs).
Seeded simulated annealing, one letter per label, fr-1600-letters 5-gram: drifted to pseudo-French because labels merge distinct key signs.
Closing formula 'vous baise tres humblement les mains' fixed A, U, M, T, R signs.
Beam search with per-label candidate sets from the key: most of f. 142 comes out as French.
Word-by-word reading of f. 142 from zoomed line images (f142_reading.txt).
f. 119 cut into 44 line images; transcription and reading by two agents with the confirmed sign list (AGENT_BRIEF.md).
Beam search with widened candidate sets and 5-gram LM (bl2.py): recovers conservation, conciliation, ferme fondement, cinq cens hommes.
Refinement pass found label corrections y=D, 8=M/N, k=A/I, U=X/R, 6=N, %=G/P; decode rerun (f119_beam3.txt).
Hand re-reading of lines 00-04, 12-14, 19, 21-22 at higher zoom; f. 119 at ~70% of signs, f. 142 ~85%.
About twenty line-by-line relabelling passes at 2x zoom with pinned letters, three lines per agent, on both letters.
Key extended in this hand: y=D/de, ✝=Q, ɤ=D/T/X, x-shape=Y/N, 3=C/D, 8=M/B/N/T, dotted Є=R, k=A, =ʃ=P.
Candidate-class phrase search over French corpora for the last unread runs (iusques icy, arrester, cherchions, faisant estat, en quoy, defaire).
Measured: f. 119 1861 signs 84 unread; f. 142 623 signs 44 unread (7 code groups); 95.1% of letter signs read.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): guise1587: f. 119 f119_glyphs.txt + f119_reading.txt, f. 142 f142_pinned.txt + f142_reading.txt; key.md (Lasry's 2022 table with this project's added values).

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): f119_reading.txt and f142_reading.txt read through. f. 142 builds sentences with scattered holes (kept read, reviewed B); f. 119 has holes or broken grammar in more than half its sentences (3% of sentences clean by docs/_check_reading.py), relabelled decoded, not read. Class read -> read in part; fraction_read 0.951 -> 0.251.

DECODE R4162 and R4165 fetched with the project cookie (b25_fetch.py): images only (Gallica views 132-133 / 155 and cipher strips), no attachment or comment; f. 120r on view 133 is another writer's clear letter (Montauban), not a copy.

f. 119 reading rebuilt word by word across line ends from f119_glyphs.txt and the bl2.py candidate values, with line images checked at ll. 00-03, 22, 37, 38, 40: 'je croy certainement' (ρ Є Δ X), 'lesquels', 'ce qu'ils pourront, je vous diray', 'je craigs trop plus les traistres que les ennemis', 'ne se doibt', 'nos amys', 'de Mercoer', 'tels subiects'. No sign label or key value changed. texts/f119_reading.md, _en.md, _reread_log.md.

Nomenclator group fbn (LES in Lasry's table) reads JE by sense in 9 of 10 places (receu, croy, tiens, vous diray, craigs, n'y espargne, vous ay mandé, ne feras, vous baise) but not at l. 22 ('[fbn] moyens'); LES is carried by fbi. Not adopted; shown [?je] and flagged for George Lasry's review.
Scored (b17_score.py, fr): 0.558 clean (24/43), explicit holes 0.698 (before 0.302). Opening, ll. 29-33 and the closing request do not build. Kept decoded, not read.

v3 verification: f. 142 reading joined into running text (f142_running_reading.md): 0.167 explicit-hole, hole rate 0.167; not workable without new key material (26 pin passes already made, f. 119's b27 re-read reached 0.558). Demoted to decoded, not read; no document of the target reads, class set to not read.
Consistency pass (cl): class not read with method 'read with known key' -> method 'not solved'; key stays partial (Lasry's table, extended).

outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit 22 Oct 2026: tokens in the documents that read as sentences, f. 142 = 623 of 2,484 (profile documents); f. 119 (1,861) is decoded, not read. texts.label: f. 119 (DECODE R4162), 27 May 1587
texts.summary: The writer (Guise?) tells Mercœur the levy of reiters is assured: by August two thousand Italian or Albanian lances and four thousand reiters; his secretary has gone to colonel Pfyffer with twelve thousand écus to treat for nine thousand Swiss; the heretics' army (eight thousand reiters, twelve thousand Swiss, lansquenets, four thousand arquebusiers for Châtillon) must be defeated, sparing nothing for the glory of God and the cause.

texts.label: f. 142 (DECODE R4165), 20 June 1587
texts.summary: After clear news of Lunebourg with nine thousand horse on the Rhine by 20 July, the cipher says the levy that was to be so far advanced is not, the thousand lances and four thousand reiters are "ung instable secours", hasty resolutions force the party to order its affairs less securely than its first designs, and within five or six days the writer hopes to settle the matter with [73], the forces going to find it at Meaux.
texts.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: f142_reading.txt joined into running text (f142_running_reading.md, line numbers and sign counts left out) scores 0.167 explicit-hole (2/12 sentences, hole rate 0.167): unread signs [?], supplied letters (est[é], tousiou[r]s, seurete[z], [n]os) and name code [73] fall in nearly every sentence; ll. 00-02, 09-10 and 13 do not build. The middle (the levy an unstable help, resolutions in haste, Meaux) reads. No contemporary decipherment; Lasry's table is the only key.
